title: Global Health Ltd - 543654 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Medanta Q2 FY27 revenue from operations rose 34% YoY to INR 14,690 million, with operating EBITDA up 60% to INR 3,701 million (25.2% margin).
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 34% YoY to INR 14,690 million and operating EBITDA grew 60% to INR 3,701 million, with margin expanding to 25.2% from 21%. PAT rose 38% YoY to INR 2,191 million. Noida, the 550-bed hospital inaugurated in November 2025, reached EBITDA breakeven in its first year. Management also approved a 500-bed Ghaziabad hospital with about INR 1,000 crore capex and reported a 4-5 year plan of over INR 6,000 crore capex with about 3,450 beds to be added. The company changed its reporting basis to revenue from operations and operating EBITDA (after ESOP, excluding other income).

segments.name: Cluster 1 (Gurugram, Indore, Ranchi)
segments.commentary: Revenue from operations INR 8,229 million (+18% YoY); operating EBITDA INR 1,810 million (+29%), margin 22%. Inpatient volumes +15%, ARPP +2%, ALOS 2.80 days (from 2.98), occupancy 66% (from 61%).

segments.name: Cluster 2 (Lucknow, Patna, Noida)
segments.commentary: Revenue from operations INR 5,790 million (+63% YoY from INR 3,547 million); operating EBITDA INR 1,837 million (+110%). Inpatient volumes +52%, ARPP +8%, occupancy 67% (from 62%). Ex-Noida inpatient volume growth about 26%.

segments.name: Medanta Noida (new, 550-bed inaugurated Nov 2025)
segments.commentary: Revenue from operations INR 1,059 million; operating EBITDA INR 86 million, achieving breakeven vs EBITDA loss of INR 199 million in Q2 FY26. Operational beds 482 after adding 49 beds in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: Expansion pipeline of 6 new greenfield hospitals including Ghaziabad; bed additions of about 3,450 over next few years, taking network to over 7,600 beds (from 3,811 operational).
Planned capex of over INR 6,000 crore over next 4-5 years, including upcoming hospitals and expansion at existing facilities.
South Delhi (GK), Mumbai, and Guwahati expected to be completed and operational around FY30; Pitampura is delayed pending revised drawings and approvals; Varanasi awaiting drawing approvals.
Near-term additions: 6 OTs and 2 cath labs at Gurugram, 4 OTs and 1 cath lab at Patna, 5 OTs at Lucknow over next couple of quarters; Lucknow OTs targeted Q3 or early Q4 FY27.
Management does not give margin guidance; Q3 expected to be seasonally softer due to festival season.
capex_capacity: Census beds 3,115 in Q2 FY27 (vs 2,658 in Q2 FY26, +17%); total operational beds 3,811 (vs 3,435).
74 beds added in the quarter: 49 at Noida and 25 at Lucknow. Occupancy 67% network-wide vs 64% a year ago.
Ghaziabad: 2.61-acre freehold parcel bought via e-auction for about INR 166 crore; Board approved 500-bed hospital with about INR 1,000 crore total capex.

Gurugram has 42 operating rooms and 7-8 cath labs; added 2 OTs and 1 biplane cath lab in Q2; Siemens ARTIS icono biplane added at Gurugram; Siemens ARTIS ceiling-mounted cath lab and VELYS hip navigation added at Patna.
Lucknow to add a new OP floor, adding about 20-30% of hospital's outpatient capacity.
demand_pricing: Inpatient volumes +30% YoY and outpatient volumes +38%; occupied bed days +22%; ALOS 2.89 days vs 3.06 days.
Management prioritises volume over tariff; ARPP growth stable (3% network), with tariff increases of 5% or less and none for several years at Patna and early years at Lucknow.
Cluster 2 payer mix about 26-27% insurance; Patna has around 19-20% CGHS (PPP project); no significant payer mix shift in Cluster 2.
ARPPs/ARPOBs by hospital not disclosed; changes described as 1-2%, driven by ALOS and mix.
Oncology drug price capping: management said impact is too early to evaluate; sees access benefits and volume offset, citing cardiac implant price capping history.

qa_highlights.question: What is Cluster 2 inpatient volume growth ex-Noida, and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Ex-Noida inpatient volume growth about 26%, with no significant payer mix shift; growth reflects doctor hiring and capacity added in prior 12-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Cluster 2 margin (about 37% ex-Noida) inflated by one-offs or cost allocation?
qa_highlights.answer: No one-off items in either year; corporate costs are loaded entirely on Gurugram (Cluster 1), so Cluster 2 carries no corporate overhead, which lifts its margin. No margin guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: Timelines for greenfield projects (South Delhi, Mumbai, Guwahati, Pitampura)?
qa_highlights.answer: South Delhi (GK) progressing, with possible 1-2 month slowdown from pollution norms; Mumbai and Guwahati approvals in place; Pitampura delayed on revised drawings. South Delhi, Mumbai and Guwahati expected around FY30.

qa_highlights.question: Will ARPP growth pick up from FY28 in developing hospitals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is keeping ARPP stable and volume-led; tariff changes will be nominal (5% or less), and the approach to clean tariffs will not change.

qa_highlights.question: Why are newer hospital occupancies higher than older ones?
qa_highlights.answer: Gurugram's large procedural base (42 OTs) means lower medical-management share and faster throughput; Cluster 2 gets more medical management work. Management suggests a 65-67% occupancy range covers fixed costs well.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for retail pharmacy and adjacencies?
qa_highlights.answer: Pharmacy, labs and clinics treated as continuity-of-care adjacencies scaled with hospitals; management sees large headroom in an unorganised market but is taking measured steps with no strategic intent beyond this.

risks_watch: Oncology drug margin capping: impact still uncertain, with court and government matters pending; management says it is too early to quantify.
Pollution-linked construction restrictions may slow South Delhi build for 1-2 months; Pitampura delayed.
Talent availability in Tier 2 cities could slow ramp-up of new hospitals, per management.
Q3 seasonality (festival season) may cause quarter-to-quarter margin variation.
Cluster-level disclosure only; hospital-level ARPP, drugs and consumables mix, and surgical vs non-surgical split not provided (follow-up promised).
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on volumes, Noida breakeven and expansion, while deflecting on margin guidance, hospital-level ARPP and oncology pricing impact, which it called too early to assess. Management stressed long-term orientation over quarterly margin trends.
key_quotes: We have delivered a strong performance this quarter.
Medanta Noida achieved EBITDA breakeven in Q2 FY27, posting revenue from operations of INR 1,059 million and operating EBITDA of INR 86 million for the quarter.
we have a significant bed addition pipeline that is expected to add approximately 3,450 beds over the next few years.
we will continue to look at treating every kind of patient.

adds.what: 500-bed Ghaziabad hospital (Board approved, INR ~1,000 cr capex; 2.61-acre parcel bought for ~INR 166 cr)
~3,450 beds over next few years across 6 greenfield hospitals (network to 7,600+ beds from 3,811 operational)
South Delhi (GK), Mumbai, Guwahati hospitals expected operational around FY30
Lucknow 5 OTs (targeted Q3 or early Q4 FY27)
Gurugram 6 OTs and 2 cath labs, Patna 4 OTs and 1 cath lab over next couple of quarters
Lucknow new OP floor (adds ~20-30% of hospital outpatient capacity)

growth.why: Q2 revenue +34% and EBITDA +60% with occupancy up to 67%, and guidance for ~3,450 new beds and >INR 6,000 cr capex over 4-5 years, but most of the new capacity is FY30-plus or approval-stage and no revenue growth number is guided, so backing is partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose to 25.2% from 21% and Cluster 2 margin ~37% ex-Noida, but management gives no margin guidance and flags Q3 as seasonally softer from festival season.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q3-Q4 FY27 near-term; FY30 for major
rows.why: Census beds 3,115 and operational beds 3,811 with 74 beds added in Q2; Lucknow 5 OTs targeted Q3/early Q4 FY27 and Gurugram/Patna OTs and cath labs over next couple of quarters, but South Delhi, Mumbai and Guwahati are expected only around FY30 and Pitampura is delayed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Inpatient volumes +30% YoY, outpatient +38%, occupied bed days +22%, and network occupancy 67% vs 64%, with Cluster 2 inpatient volumes +52% (about +26% ex-Noida).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Board approved a 500-bed Ghaziabad hospital at about INR 1,000 cr (2.61-acre parcel bought for about INR 166 cr), and a 4-5 year plan of over INR 6,000 cr capex was outlined; occupancy at 67% is below the 80%+ level that would trigger a new announcement on utilisation alone.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gives no revenue or margin guidance numbers, and ARPP growth is stable at 3% with tariff increases of 5% or less, so there is no explicit guide to raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Oncology drug price capping impact is unquantified, South Delhi may slow 1-2 months from pollution norms, Pitampura is delayed, and Tier 2 talent availability could slow new hospital ramp-up.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management mentions pharmacy, labs and clinics as continuity-of-care adjacencies with measured steps, but no specific product or service launch date was given; OPD pharmacy revenue is already +53% to INR 699 million.

rows.label: Noida breakeven and ramp-up of 550-bed hospital
rows.why: Medanta Noida reached EBITDA of INR 86 million in Q2 vs a loss of INR 199 million a year earlier, with 482 operational beds after adding 49 in the quarter.

rows.label: International patient revenue growth
rows.why: International patient revenue rose 30% YoY to INR 993 million in Q2 FY27.

rows.label: Oncology drug price capping
rows.why: Management calls impact too early to evaluate, with court and government matters pending, and cites access benefits and volume offsets from past cardiac implant price capping.

tone.note: Management was confident on volumes, Noida breakeven and expansion, and stressed long-term orientation; it deflected on margin guidance, hospital-level ARPP and the oncology pricing impact, which analysts pressed on.
